summary: 14-day analysis of Nightscout telemetry and AAPS profile data demonstrates exceptional glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), a mean glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%), and zero readings below 70 mg/dL. Basal rates, Insulin Sensitivity Factors (ISF), Carbohydrate Ratios (CR), and Duration of Insulin Action (DIA) are well-calibrated across all daily time segments. Postprandial glucose excursions are minimal during weekday meals, with a mild peak (up to 188 mg/dL) observed after weekend brunches that resolves smoothly within 4 hours under normal loop operation.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM telemetry is complete across the 14-day analysis period with 1,345 entries, 100% coverage, and zero data gaps. Active AAPS profile and declared meal strategies are present.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 valid entries spanning 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-21. 32 treatment entries including 28 meal boluses and 4 temporary target events.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall control is exceptionally safe with negligible hypoglycemia risk and low variability.
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean glucose: 117.0 mg/dL; SD: 15.1 mg/dL; CV: 12.9%; TIR: 99.7%; TAR: 0.3%; TBR: 0.0%. Minimum recorded glucose was 70.0 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal rates maintain flat glucose profiles overnight (102-107 mg/dL) and during fasting windows. Target segments (90-115 mg/dL) are appropriate and safe.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local mean glucose remains stable overnight between 00:00 and 06:00 (102.3 to 115.2 mg/dL) without persistent nocturnal drift.

analysis_steps.findings: CR segments (9-12 g/U) and ISF segments (40-48 mg/dL/U) are well matched to user requirements. DIA of 5.5 hours correctly reflects active insulin decay.
analysis_steps.evidence: 24 therapy response windows show postprandial glucose returning to baseline within 240-360 minutes without secondary hypoglycemic rebound.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are active and functioning effectively to assist postprandial recovery without causing excessive IOB accumulation.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific SMB activation condition switches (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled) evaluate to null in profile export and require manual verification in AAPS.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits for max basal (2.4 U/h) and max IOB (8.0 U) provide sufficient operational headroom while maintaining strong safety boundaries.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal set to 2.4 U/h (~2.3x max scheduled basal of 1.05 U/h); max IOB set to 8.0 U; Dynamic ISF factor at 100%.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens and Dynamic Sensitivity boolean toggles return null in profile raw settings.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared weekday meal strategies (20 min prebolus, 70% immediate) achieve strong control. Weekend brunches show a higher 120-minute peak (188 mg/dL) due to high-fat meal composition.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekday breakfast 120m rise averages +33 to +57 mg/dL; weekend brunch 120m rise averages +62 to +70 mg/dL, returning to baseline by 240m.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared e-carbs (20g over 120 min) for weekend brunches appropriately model extended absorption without requiring manual correction boluses.
analysis_steps.evidence: 24 therapy response windows show complete return to starting glucose levels by 360 minutes after meals.

analysis_steps.findings: All core profile parameters (basal, CR, ISF, DIA, targets) are verified as stable and optimal. No profile parameter adjustments are recommended. Minor optimization can be achieved by fine-tuning prebolus timing for mixed high-fat weekend brunches.
analysis_steps.evidence: Consensus across all 8 workflow stages showing 99.7% TIR, 0% TBR, and stable fasting glucose.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Verification needed for AAPS activation flags currently returning null values.

strengths: Outstanding Time in Range (99.7%) across the entire 14-day evaluation period.
Zero time spent in hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) and extremely low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%).
Overnight basal calibration maintains continuous stability between 100 mg/dL and 110 mg/dL.
Effective prebolus execution for weekday meals preventing sharp postprandial spikes.
issues: Transient postprandial glucose peak reaching 188 mg/dL at 120 minutes following high-fat weekend brunches.

recommendations.title: Maintain Current Profile Settings
recommendations.description: Current basal rates, CR, ISF, and DIA are performing at an exceptional level of safety and efficiency. No changes to basal, CR, ISF, or targets are necessary.

recommendations.title: Verify Local AAPS SMB Activation Switches
recommendations.description: Confirm that specific SMB activation conditions (e.g. SMB with COB, SMB after carbs) are explicitly enabled in the local AAPS app preferences, as export telemetry returned null for these sub-flags.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Overall metrics demonstrate exceptional control with 99.7% Time in Range, 0.0% Time Below Range, and a mean glucose of 117.0 mg/dL. The current basal segments, carb ratios, sensitivity factors, and DIA are perfectly aligned with user requirements.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Conduct a routine overnight fasting basal check during the next sensor session to re-confirm baseline stability.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA profile settings unchanged.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain a 15–20 minute pre-bolus with a ~70% immediate upfront bolus for standard weekday meals, supported by active SMB/UAM and declared e-carbs for complex high-fat meals.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Standard meals show excellent 2-to-4 hour recovery. Higher fat weekend brunches generate a transient peak at 120 minutes (188 mg/dL) that resolves smoothly by 240 minutes, indicating meal composition dynamics rather than a CR deficit.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe 120-minute postprandial glucose peaks during weekend brunches when extending the pre-bolus time from 10 to 15-20 minutes.

exceptions.suggestion: Extend pre-bolus timing to 15-20 minutes or increase upfront immediate bolus percentage slightly (from 60% toward 70%) while keeping declared 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes.
exceptions.rationale: Higher fat and protein content delays carbohydrate absorption, leading to a temporary postprandial peak (188 mg/dL) at 120 minutes.

implementation_steps: Verify local AAPS settings to confirm specific SMB condition toggles and Autosens configuration.
Maintain all active profile basal rates, carb ratios, sensitivity factors, and target ranges.
Test extending the pre-bolus time from 10 to 15-20 minutes for mixed high-fat weekend brunches.
Monitor postprandial glucose at 120 minutes following weekend brunches to confirm reduction of the peak excursion below 160 mg/dL.
education: High-fat and high-protein meals delay gastric emptying, which can cause glucose peaks to appear 2 to 3 hours after eating rather than in the first hour.
Pre-bolus timing aligns the peak action of rapid-acting insulin with the initial entry of glucose into the bloodstream, reducing peak postprandial excursions.
safety_notes: This output is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice.
All proposed settings or meal strategy adjustments must be independently verified and approved by your healthcare provider.
Make changes one at a time and monitor glucose levels closely following any change.
